newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IFCI to cut prime rate to 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: India's IFCI to cut prime rate to 15 pct.

text.p: The Industrial Finance Corporation of India Ltd (IFCI) said on Tuesday that it had decided to reduce its prime lending rate to 15 percent from 16 percent, effective on May 1.

IFCI said the decision to cut its prime rate was in reaction to the Reserve Bank of India's slack season credit policy, which it said "contains many salutary measures that would impel a general downturn in interest rates".
It said in a statement that disbursements were provisionally estimated at 51.59 billion rupees for 1996/97 (April-March), representing of 13.1 percent rise over the previous fiscal year.
IFCI's sanctions for 1996/97 totalled 72.12 billion rupees. "During 1996/97, project finance accounted for 64.14 billion rupees and financial services 7.98 billion rupees," it said.
The major "thrust areas" of lending were power, steel, textiles, plastics, paper and paper products, fertilisers, synthetic fibres, electrical machinery, basic chemicals and machinery.
These sectors accounted for 72 percent of IFCi's sanctions in 1996/97, the statement said.
